requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to helpdesk@branch.test reaches both alice and bob local mailboxes on node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 submitted helpdesk mail successfully, and node1 directly recorded delivery to both mailboxes. A fresh post-restart submission also reached both recipients.

requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to accounts@branch.test reaches bob only.
requirements.summary: The accounts marker appeared once in bob's mailbox and not in alice's. This behavior was demonstrated again after both nodes restarted.
Two genuinely nonexistent recipients were rejected at RCPT with SMTP 550 User unknown, including a final post-restart test.

requirements.requirement: Relaying for unrelated domains is rejected.
requirements.summary: Node1 rejected example.net recipients at RCPT with SMTP 554 Relay access denied, including after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the sample message and routing handover under /srv/legacy2/smtp-alias-delivery.
requirements.summary: The final node1 contents and SHA-256 hashes for aliases.txt and sample.eml match the preparation baseline and survived node1's restart. No executor command modified the corresponding node2 directory.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. Node1 used the CentOS repository's Postfix 3.8.5 package, which was active after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end SMTP evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart observation and acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered connectivity and delivery behavior. Hygiene is reduced only by one misdirected test message and two retained reboot log files.
limitations: The handover files were directly rehashed after execution only on node1. Preservation on node2 is supported by its preparation baseline and the absence of any executor command targeting that directory, rather than by a final node2 hash observation.
The retained root-mailbox test message was not explicitly inspected in the final snapshot, although direct delivery was recorded and no removal command appears later in the timeline.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was focused and ended with healthy package state, no failed services, and only the required SMTP listener added. One unnecessary test mutation occurred: cmd-4d869d2490bd4962 submitted to nobody@branch.test, which was actually a valid system account and delivered into root's mailbox; no cleanup was shown, so that message appears retained. The mandatory restart commands also left small /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log files on both nodes; their creation supported the restart protocol, but the retained files are avoidable residue. The initial Postfix startup failure was diagnosed and corrected, so it is not treated as an unnecessary mutation or final defect.
